holidays.name: International Kissing Day (World Kiss Day)
holidays.description: A day dedicated to puckering up. Smooch a sweetheart, a friend, a kid, or even your very patient dog. It's a worldwide excuse to celebrate the humble kiss in all its forms.
holidays.origin: The exact origin is unclear. It's an unofficial observance that is said to have started in the United Kingdom and has since spread worldwide.
holidays.funFact: The scientific study of kissing has its own name: philematology. Researchers say a passionate kiss can burn a few calories per minute and may involve dozens of facial muscles.

holidays.name: National Fried Chicken Day
holidays.description: A crispy, golden, finger-licking tribute to one of the most beloved comfort foods on the planet. Grab a drumstick, skip the silverware, and embrace the crunch.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday of unclear origin. It joins the long list of American food days that celebrate favorite dishes.
holidays.funFact: Scottish immigrants are often credited with bringing the tradition of frying chicken in fat to the American South. Enslaved West African cooks then added seasonings that shaped the dish we know today.

holidays.name: Take Your Webmaster to Lunch Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the person who keeps your website running, fixes broken links at odd hours, and never gets enough credit. Buy them a meal. They have earned it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial workplace observance of unclear origin. It was created to recognize the people behind the scenes of the internet.
holidays.funFact: The first website went live in 1991 and was created by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN. That makes the very first webmaster a physicist.
